change: On-the-fly augmentation of training slices: rotation +-15 deg, scale 0.9-1.1, intensity shift +-0.1, light elastic (alpha 10 px, sigma 4). No horizontal flip. One sampled geometric transform is applied identically to all input channels and the GT.
hypothesis: Train Dice 0.95 vs val 0.82 by epoch 16 indicates overfitting on 15 patients. Augmentation should narrow the train/val gap and raise validation Dice, chiefly for esophagus and trachea.

comparison_to_parent.interpretation: Augmentation narrowed the train/val gap (val present-only 0.506/0.838/0.089 vs train 0.628/0.851/0.023 at epoch 24; E014 no-aug gap was ~0.21/0.16/0.18) and improved heart (+0.075) and slightly esophagus (+0.030) over E001, but trachea collapsed (-0.296, 0.081 vs 0.377) and foreground mean fell below E001 (0.534 vs 0.598): the elastic term destroys the thin trachea.

notes: Run locally on MPS after a DataLoader shared-memory crash at epoch 4; retrained with num_workers=0 (throughput-only change).

Elastic augmentation was mis-scaled (alpha applied in normalized grid units -> up to ~600 px warp on 512 px images), suppressing all organ learning in the first completed run; fixed _sample_elastic_displacement to pixel units and retrained. Validated by a 5-epoch A/B (heart val present-only 0.535 vs 0.618 no-aug at e4).
Aorta absent from segthor_part1, reported as n/a.

what_to_check: Train/val Dice gap vs E001 (should narrow): narrowed — val present-only 0.506/0.838/0.089 vs train 0.628/0.851/0.023 at epoch 24; heart essentially closes the gap.
Foreground mean 3D Dice vs E001 (0.598): 0.534, below E001 (-0.064); augmentation did not beat the baseline overall.

HD95 not worse; elastic on thin trachea could hurt: HD95 worse than E014 on all organs (esophagus 19.99, heart 49.80, trachea 57.28 mm); trachea collapsed (Dice 0.081, HD95 57.28) — elastic hurts the thin trachea as feared.
Follow-up question from the plan: does 50 epochs with augmentation beat 25 without? Open — not tested here.
